request.prompt: A creature sprite for RimWorld: the noolim, a darting shoal of dull silver slivers from the dark floor of the Twilight, seen as a shoal and never as one individual. The shoal is an irregular, swirling, open cloud of about twenty separate slivers, with three or four strays drifting just outside the main spread. Every sliver is the same shape: a long, thin, sharply pointed shard of dull silver with a flat narrow cross-section, a crisp painted edge, a thin dark contour line of its own and a dull metallic glint along one edge. Shading is restrained and painterly, in flat-to-two-tone strokes. The slivers have no fin, no tail and no head. They sit at many different angles and depths, streaming and turning together as if darting through water, with clear gaps of transparent background between neighbours. The cloud keeps the same compact oval envelope and the same sliver shape in every facing. Front view (south): seen head-on, the same thin shards point their sharp tips toward the viewer and appear foreshortened as narrow pointed silver flecks, scattered at varied angles, with the same thinness, dark contour and metallic glint as the side view. Rear view (north): seen from behind, the same thin shards recede away from the viewer with their blunt trailing ends toward the viewer, foreshortened as narrow pointed silver flecks at varied angles, in the same oval envelope and at the same width as the front view, with the same thin shape, dark contour and finish. Side views (east and west): the thin shards lie side-on as long slender silver slivers at varied angles in a loose layer with open space showing through the centre, all swept the same way along the direction of travel. Colouring is dull, unlit silver with a deeper shade of the local colour along the edges. Realistic painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style with clean dark outlines. Exactly ONE shoal, centred, the whole cloud visible with nothing cut off. Fully transparent background: no ground, no water, no shadow, no text, no border.
